thread:
alexander: Heads-up: multiple SEs flagged a customer in us-west reporting 4-6x p99 for text-generation calls since ~09:10 PST. p95 up ~60%. Seeing TLS handshake tail. digging now.

maria_chen: on it — can you paste a sample request id or trace? which model/route?

alexander: request ids: req_6e9f2a, req_6e9f9b. Route: /v1/generate -> model:redwood-1-large hosted-us-west. SE says retries stack up and errors occasionally time out.

support-bot: Customer ticket #43218 created by SE team: "us-west latency + intermittent 524s". Attached logs from customer, sample curl, and timeline.

sam_w: I pulled metrics from observability: spike starts at 09:09:12, TLS handshake time (server side accept latency) jumps from ~8ms -> 220ms p99. TCP connect stable. Trace suggests cross-az hop increased for some clients.

jordan_k: Any DNS anomalies? If client hitting a different POP could cause handshake backoff.

alexander: ran quick dig from our probe in us-west1: 
```
;; ANSWER SECTION:
us-west.api.redwood.dev. 60 IN A 35.201.12.78
```
TTL still 60. But traceroute from customer shows a detour: 
```
traceroute to 35.201.12.78 (35.201.12.78), 30 hops max
 1  10.1.0.1  1.2 ms
 2  core-us-west-2  4.3 ms
 3  cr-cr-2  120.5 ms  <-- big hop
 4  edge-us-west  4.6 ms
```

maria_chen: that 120ms hop is suspicious — could be a transient ISP path or provider flap. Any BGP updates around 09:09?

sam_w: checking BGP updates... I see a short withdrawal/announce for our anycast prefix at 09:08:58 affecting a subset of peers. Short-lived (~40s) but enough to cause path shift.

li_patel: ops-bot just alerted on route changes and rebalances in the region at 09:09. logs: `route-manager: anycast-rebalance triggered for prefix 35.201.12.0/24 -> candidate POP us-west-2b`

ops-bot: [alert] anycast-rebalance started at 09:08:59, reason: peer flapping from upstream ASNs, action: shift announce to us-west-2b for capacity/affinity.

jordan_k: That matches. When anycast shifts, some clients may hit a POP that's further network-wise causing TLS RTT spike during handshake. Should be transient but explains p99.

alexander: customer reports >10min of bad tail. We need to reduce customer impact: options = rollback announce to previous POP, add local BGP prepends to steer, or temporary degrade to lower-CPU model variant (reduces server-side processing time but handshake still heavy). Thoughts?

maria_chen: Short-term: rollback the rebalance for affected prefixes to restore path affinity. Also raise DNS TTL to 30s? TTL is already 60. Changing TTL won't help immediate flows.

sam_w: rollback is doable but must coordinate with eng-infra because the rebalance was triggered by upstream flap; we should avoid oscillation. Suggest: rollback plus increase monitoring windows and enable sticky routing for class-of-service for the impacted customer while we stabilize BGP.

li_patel: I can flip rollback for those specific prefixes now and pin them to us-west-1 POP for 30m. Doing a partial rollback minimizes global churn. Will coordinate with oncall.

ops-bot: [command] route-manager rollback --prefix 35.201.12.0/24 --target-pop us-west-1 --duration 1800s

ops-bot: rollback accepted, marker id rm-20240503-0915, starting now.

alexander: nice — can we also add a short-term L7 route policy to prefer connections with lower TLS RTT? maybe fallback to local POP if handshake > 200ms?

jordan_k: we can enable early-fallback policy in the load-balancer: if TLS handshake takes > 180ms on the first attempt, try alternate POP (with circuit breaker). But be careful with retry amplification.

maria_chen: I'll prepare a canary for that policy scoped to the impacted customer and a few test tokens. Not rolling wide.

support-bot: Noted: set expectation with customer that we're actively rolling back route changes and enabling fallback. SE updated ticket #43218.

sam_w: telemetry already showing improvement after rollback started: p99 TLS handshake down to ~30ms within 90s for most clients. A few still see tails — probably cached sessions or TCP sockets stuck.

li_patel: completed rollback. rm-20240503-0915 -> success. No further BGP withdrawals in last 2m.

alexander: For follow-up: run postmortem to capture root cause (upstream AS flapping triggered our anycast rebalance) and add mitigations: 1) smoother rebalance with hysteresis, 2) per-customer sticky routing for SLA tiers, 3) playbook for rollback + L7 fallback.

jordan_k: also add tests to simulate upstream withdraws in staging and observe our rebalance behavior, ensure we don't create long-lasting tail latencies.

maria_chen: I'll draft the incident blameless summary and include graphs (p50/p95/p99, BGP events timeline, traceroutes).

support-bot: SE notified customer and offered a credit pending postmortem. Customer satisfied for now, keeping ticket open until postmortem.

alexander: thanks all. I'll add the reproduction steps to the ticket: how to run traceroute/dig from affected client, sample trace IDs, and commands we used. Closing the loop after the write-up. :thumbsup:
